findings.title: Embedded-post author link uses the inverted lightness pair
findings.body: This rule previously used `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`, but the new dark/light selection uses primary 70% and secondary 30%. That reverses the intended mapping in both themes: the light theme changes from the existing 30% tone, while the dark-theme link is rendered with a much darker secondary-derived color that can lack contrast against the embedded-post background. Preserve the original light branch and use the corresponding dark branch: primary 30% and secondary 70%.

findings.title: Mobile custom-message counter reverses its intended lightness values
findings.body: The previous color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, but this replacement selects primary 30% in light themes and secondary 70% in dark themes. This is the opposite of the intended primary/secondary lightness pairing and changes the existing light-theme appearance. It should select primary 70% for light themes and secondary 30% for dark themes, matching the desktop modal rule.

findings.title: Mobile topic-map heading no longer preserves its original emphasis
findings.body: The topic-map `h3` previously used primary at 20% lightness, but the new expression changes it to 50% in light themes and uses secondary 50% in dark themes. This makes the heading substantially less emphasized on light themes and does not apply the expected secondary 80% dark-theme counterpart. Use primary 20% with secondary 80% instead.

findings.title: Desktop group-member names were changed to the title color
findings.body: `.group-member-info .name` previously used primary at 30% lightness, whereas this change makes it use the same 50%/50% pair as `.title`. That unnecessarily dims names in light themes and selects the wrong dark-theme tone. The name should retain primary 30% for light themes and use secondary 70% for dark themes.

findings.title: Mobile group-member names use the wrong lightness pair
findings.body: The mobile `.group-member-info .name` had primary at 30% lightness before this change, but it now uses a 50%/50% pair copied from the title styling. This changes the light-theme name color and gives dark themes the wrong secondary-derived tone. It should use primary 30% and secondary 70%, as required for the corresponding name style.
